comment: Mutation testing for the SHIPPED RUNTIME assembly. A THIRD config because Stryker mutates one 'project' per run. Registry members, MapConfig, the IDwarfMapper facade and the exception types have no derivable case-space the way an attribute does — there is no AttributeUsage to decompose and no endpoint matrix to cross them against — so a surviving mutant is the only non-textual proof that a case is untested. This is what makes AmbiguousInterfaces and DestinationType (zero references in any test family, round 18) impossible rather than merely noticed. Run via scripts/housekeeping.ps1 -Mutation, and nightly in CI via the 'mutation' matrix job (leg: runtime) in .github/workflows/ci.yml (needs: dotnet tool install -g dotnet-stryker --version 4.16.0). MEASURED 2026-08-17 on Stryker 4.16.0, against the WHOLE test suite (5,650 tests): score 61.02 % (72 detected of 118 scoreable — 71 killed + 1 timeout; 39 survived, 7 uncovered, 8 compile errors excluded), 12 min 25 s wall-clock on 12 cores. break is that score rounded DOWN to 61. THE NUMBER WENT DOWN FROM 66 AND MUST NOT BE 'RESTORED': 66 (a measured 66.95 % on 2026-08-16) was INFLATED by load-induced timeouts, not lost to a regression. Stryker computes 'total timeout = initialTestTime + additional-timeout', the initial serial run of this suite is ~193 s, and the default additional-timeout is a handful of seconds — so the ceiling sat only seconds above the workload. Because DwarfMapperRegistry is a process-wide static populated by module initializers and DwarfRefContext is threaded through every reference-preserving map, essentially the WHOLE suite 'covers' those two files, so each of their mutants re-ran a ~193 s workload under a ~193 s ceiling. Any concurrent build tipped it over, and Stryker records Timeout — which it COUNTS AS DETECTED. Proof that those were not real detections: of the 11 timeouts in that run, FOUR delete 'ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull' calls (lines 200-202) or turn 'Source.GetHashCode() * 397' into '/ 397' (line 301) — no loop, no recursion, no blocking call, so they CANNOT hang — and a FIFTH (DwarfRefContext line 77, 'maxDepth < 1' -> 'maxDepth <= 1') is a provably EQUIVALENT mutant: the two forms differ only at maxDepth == 1 and agree there anyway, since the original falls through 'maxDepth > AbsoluteMaxDepth' (1000) and also yields 1. No test can EVER detect it, yet 66.95 % counted it as detected. The bias has a mechanism: Stryker's bail is on by default, so a mutant WITH a killer aborts at its first failing test while a mutant nothing kills must run the entire covering set to completion — the slowest session, hence the likeliest to time out. The old Timeout bucket therefore preferentially collected SURVIVORS and reported them as detected. THE FIX IS THE CLOCK, NOT THE COVERAGE: 'additional-timeout' is raised to 120000 ms, a ~62 % cushion over the ~193 s suite instead of ~2 %. Seven of the eleven then resolve honestly as Survived and four as Killed, giving 61.02 %. That figure is corroborated independently: a run scoped to only the 288 tests that ever kill anything produced the SAME 61.02 %, twice — so 61.02 % is the property of the mutants, not of how many tests ran. Treat 61 as the ratchet floor and raise it only by killing survivors; the 13 concrete holes behind it are catalogued in Issues/ledgers/E3-E1-report.md. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-21 (round-21 T7, same Stryker 4.16.0, whole suite, quiet machine): score 87.61 % (99 killed of 113 scoreable; 12 survived, 2 no-coverage, 0 timeouts, 8 compile errors excluded), 11 min 36 s wall-clock, so break moves 61 -> 87 (87.61 floored) per the upward-ratchet-with-measurement rule. The 26.6 pp rise is real kills, not clock artifacts - ZERO timeouts under the 120 s cushion: rounds 20-21 added the interface-lookup and update-table test families (RegistryInterfaceLookupTests, RegistryUpdateContractTests, the update-side torture mirrors), and round-21 T7 killed the three C6-named survivors (registry duplicate-Register/InterfaceMaps mirror invariant; DwarfMappingDepthException ctor+message; DwarfMapMissingException.FormatMessage iterator-vs-declare fork) and added the CsCheck registry contract properties. The scoreable count also moved 118 -> 113: the deleted ResetForTests took its 5 NoCoverage mutants with it (D-b ruling) while interface lookup added new scoreable code. The Key.Equals '&&' -> '||' mutant (Key.Equals, L282 at this measurement) SURVIVES DELIBERATELY - ruled equivalent in practice (round-20 CF 5.4): it diverges only on an engineered hash collision with exactly one matching key component, which no honest test produces; do not chase it. 'low' is raised alongside break because Stryker 4.16 refuses low < break outright WITH EXIT CODE 0 (measured in round-21 H1 on the doctooling leg) - a config where low lags break makes the leg silently unrunnable. The two paragraphs above this one describe the 2026-08-17 measurement and the 66-timeout-inflation post-mortem; they are HISTORY kept because the mechanism (load-induced timeouts counting as detections) is the thing that must not be reintroduced, and 66 must still not be 'restored' - the floor is measured, not inherited. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-21 (round-22 P2, same Stryker 4.16.0, whole suite, quiet machine, StrykerOutput/2026-08-21.23-10-31): score 96.46 % (109 killed of 113 scoreable; 3 survived, 1 no-coverage, 0 timeouts, 8 compile errors excluded), 8 min 08 s wall-clock, so break moves 87 -> 96 (96.46 floored) and low with it; 'high' raised 90 -> 97 to stay above 'low' (Stryker requires low <= high the same way it requires break <= low). The rise is the P2 kill list landing: the Map/Update null-guard deletions (E3-E1 holes 3, 2) now die on ArgumentNullException+ParamName pins, the three remedy string tails (hole 11 remainder) on extended message assertions, and the TryEnterNode no-coverage mutant (hole 10) on direct DwarfRefContextOnStackGuardTests. The FOUR remaining undetected mutants are all dispositioned, none chaseable with an honest test: Key.Equals '&&' -> '||' (L282) SURVIVES DELIBERATELY - ruled equivalent in practice (round-20 CF 5.4, above); the facade TryGet guard '&&' -> '||' (IDwarfMapper.cs L73) is PROVEN equivalent (TryGetValue's out-contract and Register's ThrowIfNull make the operands co-vary - Issues/ledgers/equivalent-mutants.md); the FormatMessage 'Count: > 1' -> '>= 1' boundary (L86) is adjudicated probably-equivalent (divergence needs a 1-element list only an off-contract direct ctor call can produce - same ledger); and the Key.Equals(object) override (L286) stays NoCoverage - reachable only by boxing a private struct, FILED as Issues/round20/TASKS.md I1 for a maintainer ruling (internal+IVT contract test, or a denominator decision). Do not chase any of the four; the leg's currently killable set is exactly the 109 already killed. WHY THERE IS NO TEST FILTER, AND WHY ADDING ONE WOULD BE A REGRESSION: Stryker 4.16 does support 'test-case-filter' (undocumented in --help; it sits beside 'test-projects' in Stryker.CLI.dll's key table and is consumed by Stryker.TestRunner.VsTest.dll), and scoping this leg to the 23 classes that currently kill something cuts it to ~3 minutes. That was measured and DELIBERATELY REJECTED. A filter is a hand-maintained LIST, and lists drift silently in the one direction nothing catches: when a test becomes the sole killer of a mutant, an exclusive filter drops that kill, the SCORE GOES UP, and coverage goes down. Worse, that list cannot be derived reliably here, and this is measured rather than feared. The 23-class list was derived from every 'killedBy' set in the 2026-08-16 report — but ELEVEN mutants in that report had an EMPTY killedBy, because they were recorded as timeouts. Any class whose only kills landed on those eleven was therefore INVISIBLE to the derivation. Fixing the timeout revealed exactly that: the corrected 2026-08-17 run credits 26 killer classes, three of which — DeepRecursionGuardRuntimeTests, DepthSafetyRuntimeTests and NoneModeCollectionDepthRuntimeTests (5 kills between them, all on the DwarfRefContext depth clamp) — are absent from the 23. They were present in the suite the whole time; the data used to derive the list simply had not recorded what they killed. In this instance no kill would have been lost, because those mutants have redundant killers — but a derivation that is blind to 3 of 26 killers is not a foundation to exclude tests on. Do not add a filter to make this leg faster; raise 'additional-timeout' if timeouts reappear, and let the leg be slow. NOTE 1: 'comment' lives OUTSIDE the 'stryker-config' object because Stryker 4.16 REJECTS unknown keys inside it — the two sibling configs kept theirs inside and could not run at all until this was found. NOTE 2: the 'mutate' globs must NOT be repo-root-relative. Stryker resolves them against the PROJECT directory (src/DwarfMapper), so 'src/DwarfMapper/Foo.cs' matches nothing, every mutant is dropped with 'Removed by mutate filter', and Stryker STILL EXITS 0 — a vacuous run that housekeeping's $LASTEXITCODE check cannot detect. That is exactly what the first measured run of this file did, and it is why Assert-MutantsWereTested (scripts/housekeeping.ps1, mirrored inline in the CI job) counts scoreable statuses in the JSON report instead of trusting the exit code. NOTE 3: there is deliberately NO 'test-projects' key. It would be INERT — Stryker discovers the solution (DwarfMapper.NET.sln) and enumerates EVERY test project in it, so such a list does not select the test set. Proof: the 2026-08-16 run executed all 5,592 tests across seven test projects while that key named only two, and DwarfMapper.Generator.Tests classes appear in killedBy — a test that never ran cannot kill. The key was removed rather than corrected, so nothing here pretends to exclude anything. NOTE 4: an earlier version of this comment claimed excluding DwarfMapper.Generator.Tests cost ZERO killed mutants, on the grounds that DwarfMapValidationException's constructors are bare ': base(...)' forwarders producing no mutants. That claim was FALSE, and it was measured on a run where the exclusion never took effect (NOTE 3), so it measured nothing. Generator.Tests holds three killer classes — TopologyOracleFuzzTests, CrossConfigFuzzTests and AutoValidateRuntimeTests — accounting for 37 kill events of which 8 are EXCLUSIVE (registry line 87; DwarfRefContext lines 77 x2, 83, 88, 114 and 130 x2). Genuinely excluding it would drop the score to 60.17 %. NOTE 5: the 44 min recorded for the 2026-08-16 run is NOT a clean measurement of this configuration and should not be quoted as the cost of running the full suite. That run shared the machine with several other builds and test runs, and the same full suite with the timeout fix completes in 12 min 25 s — also on a busy machine. Contention, not test count, accounts for most of the difference; the covering-set explosion is real but it is a ~12-minute problem, not a ~44-minute one. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-23 (round-24 kill program, Stryker 4.16.0, whole suite - 8,038 tests): score 97.48 % (116 killed of 119 scoreable; 2 survived, 1 uncovered, 0 timeouts), so break moves 96 -> 97 and low 96 -> 97 with it; high stays 97. THE DENOMINATOR SHRANK 129 -> 119, AND THAT IS THE STORY. A repo-wide reformat had rewritten MapConfig's ten fluent members from 'X => this;' to 'X { return this; }'. An expression body offers Stryker nothing to remove; a block does, so the conversion minted ten new block/statement-removal mutants in a type that is COMPILE-TIME ONLY - the generator reads MapConfig method bodies syntactically and never executes them, so no runtime test can reach those blocks, and every one landed as NoCoverage. The leg measured 93.02 % before this program and 93.80 % after its one honest kill, with a hard ceiling of 123/129 = 95.35 % - break 96 had become mathematically unreachable through no change in behaviour or test quality. Collapsing those ten members back to expression bodies (src/DwarfMapper/MapConfig.cs, the ONLY formatting revert made, and made because the file is never executed) removed the artefacts and the leg scores 97.48 %, above its previous best of 96.46 %. The one remaining kill was DwarfMapExceptions L94 '{ Count: > 1 }' -> '{ Count: >= 1 }', which OVERTURNS a round-22 P2 'probably-equivalent' adjudication: the one-interface case is expressible and now asserts the ordinary 'No DwarfMapper map is registered' message instead of the ambiguous-interface one. The two surviving mutants stay adjudicated: Key.Equals's '&&' -> '||' is ruled-in-practice equivalent (round-20 CF 5.4 - ConcurrentDictionary compares hashcode before calling Equals, so a half-match cannot resolve a wrong pair), and IDwarfMapper L73.
